name: Maclura

project_scope.target_zone_status: HISTORIC_RANGE_UNRESOLVED; species native to parts of Texas but planted throughout state

look_here_first: Glossy alternate entire leaves + often sharp axillary thorn + white latex from existing natural break; don't depend on large fruit because only female plants produce it. Female trees can produce seedless green syncarps without a male nearby, but not viable seeds. Male trees have male flower heads and no huge fruit.

quick_field_key.decision: Fruit present and orange-sized lumpy green sphere?
quick_field_key.then: Maclura pomifera likely; examine its many surface units and attached branch to confirm.
Go to alternate simple entire shiny leaves, check stout pointed axillary thorn or thorn base, then latex on existing damage. Male trees or young trees can be fruitless.

quick_field_key.decision: Toothed/lobed leaves and elongated mulberry fruits?
quick_field_key.then: Morus rubra/M. alba rather than Osage orange.

quick_field_key.decision: Compound leaves or prickles over bark rather than one axillary thorn at node?
Small separate drupes, asymmetrical 3-veined leaf base?

photo_lesson.title: Osage orange — one tree, two flower sexes, giant multiple fruit
photo_lesson.subtitle: Look for alternate entire leaf and thorn without the fruit; huge syncarp identifies female fruiting trees. Real photo sources with licenses attached; arrows not yet verified.
photo_lesson.memory_rule: SHINY smooth-edged leaf + THORN + WHITE LATEX. FEMALE: softball-sized green, bumpy multiple fruit; MALE: flower heads but no huge green fruit.

field_cautions: Without fruit, look at thorn, leaf and latex together; some male/cultivar twigs can be thornless.
Do not call an entire large green sphere a single fruit of one flower; each bumpy unit derives from compact inflorescence.
Male versus female heads are different reproductive structures; do not mislabel young spherical female head as an immature whole fruit without confirmation.
Hays County observations can be planted/naturalized; strict native historical origin is unresolved.
Do not invent arrows or claim a thorn is visible until inspecting actual image.
Female fruit formation without male pollen can be seedless. Viable seed set requires pollination; never call a nearby-male requirement for merely seeing fruit.

diagnostic_photo_requirements: Closeup of pointed axillary thorn and nearby bud on same twig with reliable arrow
Thornless male specimen showing alternate leaf nodes and white latex from existing break
Female head-to-mature fruit progression on comparable branch
Morus rubra versus M. alba versus Maclura matched leaf shape / fruit without cultivar confusion
Pair a real macro of single stout thorn from leaf axil with an image of an unarmed or thornless cultivated shoot, annotate only after verified photo geometry.
